chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Maghra', from al-Halbi, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony of the son for his father, and of the father for his son, and of the brother for his brother, is valid.'
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a son or father valid for each other in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), which clarifies that the general prohibition against close kin testifying for one another does not apply to fathers, sons, and brothers. This exception is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it prioritizes the reliability of immediate family bonds over the presumption of bias in specific legal contexts. The hadith underscores the flexibility of evidentiary rules within the Ja'fari school, allowing for familial testimony where it is most naturally expected.

en.hubeali: Muhammad  Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Al Magra, from Al Halby who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is allowed, the testimony of the son for his father, and of the father for his son, and of the brother for his brother’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from abu al-Mighra’ from al-Halabiy who has narrated the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘The testimony of a father for his son, the testimony of a son for his father and the testimony of a brother for his brother is permissible.’”
